# @zakkster/lite-cellular

> Zero-GC Worley/cellular noise for 2D. `cellular2(x, y, out?)` returns the two nearest feature-point distances `f1`/`f2` and the F1 owner's cell `id`, written into a caller-owned out-struct -- **no allocation on the query path.** v1.0.0 ships the three distance metrics (euclidean/manhattan/chebyshev, fixed at instance creation) and the module free-function surface; the field baker + exact tileable wrap land in v1.1.0. Sibling of `@zakkster/lite-noise` (gradient noise); the two compose at the app layer, never in the same file.

## API

Named exports (v1.0.0): `createCellular`, `Cellular`, `cellular2`, `seedCellular`,
`VERSION`, `METRIC_EUCLIDEAN`, `METRIC_MANHATTAN`, `METRIC_CHEBYSHEV`.

```ts
// Distance metric ids. 0 (euclidean, default), 1 (manhattan), 2 (chebyshev).
// Anything else throws at construction -- the guard accepts 0/1/2 and widens the
// set from v0.1.0, it never loosens (fail-closed).
const METRIC_EUCLIDEAN: 0;
const METRIC_MANHATTAN: 1;
const METRIC_CHEBYSHEV: 2;

// Package version, in lockstep with package.json + llms.txt (three-place sync).
const VERSION: string;

interface CellularResult { f1: number; f2: number; id: number; }
interface CellularOptions { metric?: number; jitter?: number; }

class Cellular {
    // Validates metric (0/1/2 else throws) and jitter (finite, [0,1] else throws)
    // ONCE, at construction, and binds ONE metric-specific kernel to this._kernel.
    // Both immutable for the instance's life. Stores scalars plus one reused
    // out-struct -- no permutation table.
    constructor(seed?: number, opts?: CellularOptions);

    // Sample the field. Returns { f1, f2, id }: nearest and second feature-point
    // distances (in this instance's metric, LINEAR units) and the F1 owner's cell
    // id (signed int32, SMI-safe, stable per Voronoi region, metric-dependent
    // owner). Writes into `out` if given (and returns it), else returns the
    // instance's reused out-struct. THROWS on non-finite x or y. Zero allocation
    // either way. `f2 - f1` (cracks) is the caller's one subtraction.
    cellular2(x: number, y: number, out?: CellularResult): CellularResult;

    // Re-seed in place. Setup cost only -- not on any hot path. Returns this.
    reseed(seed: number): this;
}

// Create an independent instance. Throws on a bad metric id or out-of-range jitter.
function createCellular(seed?: number, opts?: CellularOptions): Cellular;

// Module free surface: euclidean, jitter 1, on a shared module seed. The
// zero-config convenience (metric/jitter control require an instance, by design).
function cellular2(x: number, y: number, out?: CellularResult): CellularResult;

// Re-seed the shared module field. Setup only; auto-seeded 0 on load. Warns once
// in dev builds when called more than once (the last caller wins); silent when
// NODE_ENV==='production'. For independent fields, give each its own createCellular.
function seedCellular(seed?: number): void;
```

## Metrics and jitter

The three metrics share ONE feature-point placement and differ only in the
distance line: euclidean `sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)` (squared in the loop, two sqrts off
it), manhattan `|dx|+|dy|`, chebyshev `max(|dx|,|dy|)` -- all in LINEAR units, so
`cheby.f <= euclid.f <= manhattan.f` holds pointwise for f1 and f2, and `f2 - f1`
stays usable as a mask/displacement. The metric is dropped from the hot loop and
bound once as `this._kernel`, so the 3x3 scan is monomorphic and branch-free.

Each grid cell scatters one feature point at `cell + 0.5 + jitter*(u-0.5)` where
`u`/`v` in `[0,1)` come from a hash of the integer cell coords + seed. `jitter` in
`[0,1]`: `0` is the exact grid of cell centres, `1` is full Worley. The bound is a
correctness precondition -- `jitter <= 1` keeps every feature point inside its cell,
which is what makes the fixed 3x3 neighbourhood scan guaranteed to contain the true
`f1`/`f2`.

Isolation (NS-01): two `createCellular` instances never cross-contaminate, and
`seedCellular` never perturbs an instance -- an instance owns its seed, the module
surface owns the shared one.

## Install

```bash
npm i @zakkster/lite-cellular
```

```js
import { createCellular, METRIC_MANHATTAN } from '@zakkster/lite-cellular';
const cell = createCellular(42, { metric: METRIC_MANHATTAN });
const c = cell.cellular2(3.5, 7.25);   // { f1, f2, id }
const cracks = c.f2 - c.f1;            // Voronoi edges, caller-side
```

## When not to use

- Full Voronoi topology (edges, vertices, adjacency, Lloyd relaxation) -- a geometry
  structure, a different library. This is the noise field, not the diagram.
- Gradient/Simplex/Perlin noise -- that is `@zakkster/lite-noise`. No overlap.
- Curl/flow off cellular -- `f1` has derivative discontinuities at cell boundaries
  by construction, so it cannot feed an analytic flow field. Use lite-noise for flow.
- Cryptographic seeding -- the hash is for reproducible scatter, not security.
- World-scale beyond ~2^52 -- past the float64 integer limit the 3x3 neighbourhood
  degenerates (the pinned v1.0.0 limit; coords up to 1e12 stay fully precise).
